title: thin-slab-vs-flow-prefetch-cost-latency-notes
summary: Working sketch comparing two allocation strategies for short-lived conversational traffic: thin-slab (slotized slabs) vs flow-prefetch (opportunistic prefetch of KV/prefixes). Focused on p50/p90/p99 latency, amortized $/query, and spillover behavior under microbursts at 1–4k QPS per shard.
key_findings: Thin-slab reduces tail amplification during sustained medium concurrency (200-600 concurrent sessions) because slotization caps per-session contended memory; p99 down by ~18% vs flow-prefetch in our mid-burst tests.

Flow-prefetch shows better average-dollar-per-query for very short, repeatable prefixes (high KV hit rate) — observed ~12–20% cost savings at KV hit >= 0.6 but with higher variance on p99 during burst overlap.

Under extreme microbursts (spike factor > 8x baseline), thin-slab exhibits predictable degradation (p99 rises smoothly) while flow-prefetch has more discontinuous tail failures due to prefetch amplification and slot thrashing.

Hybrid policy (thin-slab baseline + selective flow-prefetch for top-10% heavy prefixes) appears promising: ~10% cost upside vs pure thin-slab with only ~3% p99 regression in the synthetic replay tests.
methodology: Synthetic traffic generated from 3 customer traces (chat, search-assist, form-fill). Each trace compressed to 10k sessions and replayed with a Poisson arrival model plus injected microburst windows. Measured endpoint latencies (server-side decode start, decode complete), KV cache hit rates, slot allocation events, and GPU utilization. Cost estimates use our internal dollars-per-GPU-hour baseline and normalized token burn model. Each experiment run 5x; reported medians and interquartile bands.

detailed_notes:
Observations and hypotheses (raw):
- Prefetch amplification: when many sessions prefetch slightly different prefixes, the aggregate KV work increases and kernel contention spikes. We saw sudden decode queue growth at the prefetch completion boundary.
- Thin-slab slot recycling keeps hot sessions bounded, but increases cold-penalty for new sessions; short-lived sessions pay ~+8ms mean cold penalty vs flow-prefetch in steady-state.
- Cost math sensitivity: flow-prefetch advantage vanishes quickly if KV hit < 0.45 or if average response length grows > +30 tokens.
- GPU utilization traces show flow-prefetch smoother utilization during steady load (good for amortization) but much spikier tail during microbursts. Thin-slab yields sharper utilization jumps but fewer prolonged tail resources.
- Hybrid policy needs good signal: top-k prefix detector with TTL and conservative fanout cap. TTL too short -> noisy prefetch churn; TTL too long -> wasted work.
unresolved_questions: What is acceptable p99 regression for customers on mid-tier SLA? (ops to confirm with sales/growth)
How to instrument prefetch fanout by prefix entropy in production without heavy overhead?
What is the practical TTL sweet spot across chat vs question-answering workloads?
